id.note: Owned by the contact section's settled id, as every id below is (SC-012). <field> is the field's contract name in kebab case, never camelCase: enquiryType's id is <anchor>__enquiry-type.

action.note: Platform-native (SC-003). The normaliser masks it as {{salt:form-action}} (README, "Fixtures"), so the rest of the form compares.

root.note: The action is platform-native (SC-003); the markup is not.

repeat.from: name, email, phone (when asked), enquiry type (two or more types), message

name.note: The field's contract name; each platform maps it to its handler (SC-003).

type.when: an input: text for name, email for email, tel for phone (SC-016)

value.when: an input redrawn after a failed send, holding what was sent; a fresh form draws none (a textarea holds it as text, a select marks its option selected)

children.note: name, email and message are required; phone per the site setting (optional: the label carries the optional span). The enquiry type select lists the site's types, its first selected by default.

elements.when: the anti-spam credentials were issued. When a captcha provider is configured, the provider's widget is native, and this challenge is drawn inside a noscript element

children.note: Its text is the per-request question, masked by the normaliser as {{salt:challenge-question}}.

value.note: Masked by the normaliser as {{salt:challenge-token}} and {{salt:form-token}}.

elements.when: the anti-spam credentials were issued (with the challenge)

elements.note: Honeypot: a label and a text input out of the tab order. Its id is <anchor>__website, shaped like every real field's (<anchor>__<field>, after its field name website, the field Next's contactFieldId(formId, 'website') draws as <formId>-website today), so the ids do not tell a scraper which field is the trap. The class salt-contact__trap stays as a hook: a form filler matches field names and ids, not classes. The input carries no value attribute; it starts empty.

attributes.name: returnTo
attributes.value: from:the path of the page the form is on

elements.note: After the honeypot, where Salt for Next.js draws it.
The sentence around the link comes from labels.privacyLine.
Always present so the live region exists before it speaks; focused after a send.

zeroState: Drawn whenever the site accepts enquiries; otherwise the contact section draws its closed message instead.

script.withoutScript: A native POST to the platform's endpoint that redirects back with the status.
script.withScript: Submits in place, fetches the anti-spam credentials (with a captcha provider, it sends the token the native widget produced), fills the status region and moves focus to it.

hooks.reason: Identifies the honeypot; salt-sr-only hides it.
The submit row; laid out by the form's gap.
Names the submit button for scripts and tests; salt-button styles it.

notes.text: The privacy line, from WordPress (SC-006); no rule yet.

The form shows a privacy line when a privacy page is set (SC-006). When a captcha provider is configured, its widget is native and the arithmetic challenge is drawn inside noscript, so a visitor without JavaScript can still send the form: the challenge's credentials exist when the page is drawn, and a correct answer is accepted in place of a provider token. How each platform issues and checks them is native form delivery (SC-003). SC-006 accepts that the arithmetic path stays open beside a captcha. Without a provider the challenge is drawn as it is.
Field names in the markup are the contract's; each platform maps them to its handler (SC-003).

The form is in the fixtures (SC-016). The action, the token values and the challenge question differ per platform or per request, so the normaliser replaces exactly those with the placeholders {{salt:form-action}}, {{salt:form-token}}, {{salt:challenge-token}} and {{salt:challenge-question}}; every other attribute and text, field types included, compares.

owes: The privacy line when a privacy page is set, and the arithmetic challenge inside noscript when a captcha provider is configured (SC-006).

Kebab-case field ids (<anchor>__enquiry-type, not <formId>-enquiryType), and the honeypot's id <anchor>__website in place of <formId>-website, which contactFieldId(formId, 'website') builds today (contact-form.tsx, SC-012).
The honeypot input draws no value attribute: defaultValue="" (contact-form.tsx) prints value="" today.
No value attribute on a fresh form's fields: defaultValue="" prints value="" today; a value only when the form is redrawn with what was sent.

formerly.note: Before the form today; a div holding a p.
names salt_contact_name, salt_contact_email, salt_contact_message, salt_contact_type; honeypot salt_hp; time trap salt_time

owes: Field, label, error and status markup as above; status after the actions, inside the form; phone field per the site setting; the ids <anchor>__form, <anchor>__<field>, <anchor>__<field>-error, <anchor>__challenge and <anchor>__status (SC-012) instead of a static id.
The privacy line as p.salt-contact__privacy before the actions (SC-006).
The honeypot as a label and input with the id <anchor>__website (SC-012), in place of salt-contact-hp, and with no value attribute: template-parts/sections/contact.php draws value="" today.

The contract's field names (name, email, phone, enquiryType, message, challengeAnswer, website, challengeToken, formToken, returnTo), mapped to its handler, in place of salt_contact_*, salt_hp and salt_time (SC-003).
Input types (text, email, tel), rows="6" on the message, autocomplete on name, email and phone, and the values sent redrawn after a failed send (SC-016).
